scope.surface: Project actions entry in the Sidebar project-scope popup and the resulting Project settings dialog

newScope: The existing Sidebar project-group state certifies grouped rows, ordering, collapse, empty rows, and per-project thread creation. It does not cover project rename, per-project grouping override, or project removal.

Web Sidebar V2 exposes a trailing project-actions control for every project-scope row and opens Project settings. Web Sidebar V1 exposes equivalent rename, grouping, and remove behavior through the project context menu.
Lynx Sidebar V1 and V2 expose project/thread creation and thread actions, but no project-management entry or mutation UI.
productLoss: On one immutable project/thread snapshot, the Web project-scope popup has one canonical project row with one project-actions control. The matching Lynx popup has the same canonical project row and zero project-actions controls.

A real Web pointer opens the complete 576x244 Project settings dialog with Project name, Grouping rule, Remove project, and Close. Lynx remains on the project-scope popup because no corresponding entry exists.

The server already supports project.meta.update and project.delete, and Lynx already persists sidebarProjectGroupingOverrides. The missing behavior is a renderer/connector product gap, not an upstream capability limitation.
harnessMismatch: Attempt one used the new state before it was classified as a thread-backed fixture, so it reached a hero state and failed project/thread identity. It receives no product attribution.

Attempt two compared renderer-specific project-scope keys: Web uses a logical environment/path key while Lynx uses the server project id. Both selected project, selected thread, canonical label, and row count matched, so the key mismatch is diagnostic rather than product loss.
intentionalPlatformDelta: Web and Lynx use different internal project-scope keys. Capture identity compares canonical project label/count plus selected project/thread and retains both raw keys for diagnostics.
Web V1 uses a context menu while V2 uses a visible trailing action. Lynx should preserve those state-appropriate entries rather than force one trigger pattern onto both layouts.
classification.evidenceBoundary: This baseline certifies Browser reachability, content, geometry, pointer input, same-snapshot identity, and the missing Lynx entry. It does not assign Native credit, does not treat full-frame pixels as a dialog-parity score, and adds no tracked screenshots.

native.reason: Native remains conservative unknown until the real project-settings entry and mutation flow exist in a production bundle.
